disposition_reason: `ipmitool bmc info` is a valid application-level request but its success is transport-agnostic unless the OS IPMI device and driver are mapped. The row's unique claim is not merely that the BMC answers; it is that the exchange traverses FPGA and BMC I2C-1 via SSIF. That can be evidenced through interface identity and transport error telemetry without mandatory probing, provided alternate IPMI routes are excluded. test_case.test_name: Test SSIF connection between FPGA and BMC I2C-1 — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify a functional host-to-BMC SSIF exchange over the named FPGA and BMC I2C-1 path by obtaining valid BMC information through the correct local IPMI transport without fallback to another interface.
required_package: Platform diagram mapping host IPMI device through FPGA to BMC I2C-1 SSIF
OS driver/module and `/dev/ipmi*` or equivalent interface corresponding to that SSIF path
Approved `ipmitool` build/interface option and sudo policy
Expected BMC Device ID, Device Revision, Firmware Revision, IPMI Version and manufacturer/product identity fields
Method to prove no KCS/BT/LAN/alternate-interface fallback
SSIF/I2C/FPGA error counters or logs, timeout and retry acceptance limits
test_case.test_command: Identify the FPGA, BMC I2C-1 and OS IPMI device/driver mapping; disable or account for alternate transport selection; capture driver/interface and error baseline; run the source read-only BMC-info request through the approved local SSIF interface; validate exit status and required identity fields; correlate SSIF/I2C/FPGA counters/logs and confirm no fallback or new errors.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.`; it becomes enforceable only after resolving: Resolve Reliability row129 Wistron-HW Robust-00007-V003: provide the authoritative mapping from the OS IPMI device/driver through FPGA to BMC I2C-1 SSIF, approved ipmitool interface and sudo policy, expected `bmc info` identity fields, proof that no KCS/BT/LAN/alternate fallback was used, and SSIF/I2C/FPGA timeout/retry/error criteria. Confirm physical probing/photos are not core acceptance unless separately approved.
safety_gate: Use only read-only BMC information requests
Confirm selected local interface and privilege scope before sudo
Do not unload drivers, alter SSIF/I2C routing, reset BMC or probe hardware for this static functional run
Bound command timeout and capture failure once without automatic retry masking an intermittent link
Preserve existing logs and compare transport-specific error deltas
expected_evidence: Platform and OS mapping from selected IPMI interface through FPGA to BMC I2C-1 SSIF
Host kernel, ipmitool, driver/module and device-node identities
Pre/post SSIF/I2C/FPGA counters and preserved relevant logs
Timestamped command, stdout/stderr, exit code and duration
Proof no alternate transport/fallback and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Wistron I2C policy requires the BMC controller/bus and expected response. Here the host command is acceptable only when platform evidence maps its local SSIF transport to FPGA and BMC I2C-1.

source_conflict.reason: The source name requires a specific FPGA/I2C-1 SSIF path, while the command does not select or prove its transport and Criteria defines no response fields. DeepSeek/GPT V2 add physical probing that is absent from the source.

blocked.reason: A safe review-layer method is defined; missing project values are runtime gates rather than a review blocker.
